clue.text: Biscuit with salt — that's a great thing

parts.note: a cracker is a thin dry biscuit
an old salt is a sailor, as is a jack (Jack Tar)

explanation.surface: Someone praises a salty biscuit as something terrific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like a seasoning but is the old word for a sailor, as is JACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackerjack is an informal word for an excellent person or thing.

clue.text: Get knotted once again!

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to tie is to make a knot

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal, repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get knotted!' is British slang for 'go away', here read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To retie is to fasten a knot again.

clue.text: Right to remove faults

definitions.meaning: a verb: to put errors right

explanation.definitionFit: Correct is both the adjective for accurate and the verb for amending errors.

clue.text: See quail fluttering draw level

indicators.note: a fluttering bird is in motion, so these letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Watching a game bird flap its wings as a match is tied.
explanation.definitionFit: To equalise is to score and bring a contest to equal scores.

clue.text: Voice emanating from chemical toilet

indicators.note: the letters come out from within the words chemical toilet

explanation.surface: A voice comes from a portable camping lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto is a vocal range, the lowest female or highest adult male singing part.

clue.text: Gap isn't complete as has been said

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the phrase is taken as it is heard

parts.note: something incomplete is not whole

explanation.surface: A remark that a gap leaves something unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: A knothole is a hole in timber where a knot has dropped out, a small gap.

clue.text: Bat has very brief sort of visit with cunning creature

parts.note: a flying visit is a very brief one
the fox is proverbially cunning

explanation.surface: A bat pays a quick call along with a crafty animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The flying fox is a large fruit bat of the tropics.

clue.text: Holding the reins of office?

parts.note: a rider holding the reins sits on horseback; figuratively one in charge

explanation.definitionFit: In the saddle is an idiom for being in a position of control or power.

clue.text: Material from the Big Apple plus western half of London

parts.note: the Big Apple is the nickname of New York, abbreviated NY

indicators.note: the western half of a word written left to right is its first three of six letters

explanation.surface: A fabric said to come from New York and part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fibre woven into cloth, a kind of material.

clue.text: Celebrity broke open some sweets

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
to burst is to break open suddenly

explanation.surface: A famous person tore open a bag of sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Starburst is a brand of fruit chews sold in packs, so some sweets.

clue.text: Unruly sot with wealthy one that cannot fly

indicators.note: unruly suggests disorder, so the letters of sot are rearranged

parts.note: wealthy means rich

explanation.surface: A drunk and a rich man are paired with a flightless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the largest flightless bird.

clue.text: Shopkeeper, first person in France to meet the Modfather

parts.note: je is French for I, the first person singular
Paul Weller, of The Jam, is nicknamed the Modfather

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper meets the singer Paul Weller in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Weller is an English singer whose mod style earned him the nickname 'the Modfather'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeweller is a trader who keeps a shop selling gems and rings.

clue.text: Hold on, it is not the winner

definitions.meaning: a runner who is merely second is ..., not first

explanation.definitionFit: Just a second is a phrase asking someone to wait, and literally a mere second place.

clue.text: Spiritual enlightenment about origin

parts.note: re means about or concerning
birth is an origin or beginning

explanation.surface: Spiritual awakening concerns where something began.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebirth is a spiritual renewal, being born again into a new outlook.

clue.text: Swells seen dancing, carrying booze that's knocked back

indicators.note: the rearranged letters carry the second piece within them
dancing moves the letters of seen about
knocked back means the word for booze is read backwards

parts.note: grog is a slang word for booze

explanation.surface: Swells at a dance carry drinks they down quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swells' looks like posh gentlemen at a dance, but it is the verb. 'dancing' gives ENES and 'knocked back' gives GORG, held by 'carrying'.
explanation.definitionFit: To engorge is to swell up, especially with blood or fluid.

clue.text: Opening to take money

parts.note: the narrow gap in a vending machine or meter into which coins are put

explanation.definitionFit: A coin slot is the narrow aperture that accepts payment in a machine.

clue.text: Larger than usual pullover, size displayed inside

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words pullover size displayed

explanation.surface: A big jumper with its size label shown inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversized means bigger than the normal size.

clue.text: Live herons? Bother!

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a siege is the collective noun for a group of herons

explanation.surface: An exclamation of annoyance about some birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bother!' looks like a mild oath but is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To besiege someone is to harass or pester them with requests.

clue.text: Waves behind ship keeping footballer clean?

parts.note: a back is a defensive football player
to wash is to clean

explanation.surface: A ship's wake keeps a footballer clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Backwash is the water pushed backwards by a vessel moving through it.

clue.text: Losing heart, the gamers destroyed what's under the stairs?

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are broken up and rebuilt
losing heart means the word the loses its central letter

explanation.surface: Discouraged gamers wreck something kept in a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing heart' cuts THE to TE; 'destroyed' shuffles TE with GAMERS.
explanation.definitionFit: In British homes the gas meter is often found in the cupboard under the stairs.

clue.text: Chopped down and fired

definitions.meaning: a tree felled with an axe
an employee dismissed from a job

explanation.definitionFit: Axed means both cut with an axe and dismissed from employment.

clue.text: Strange aroma round public house initially could be pot

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the other piece
strange suggests something odd, so the letters of aroma are reordered
initially takes the first letters of public and house

explanation.surface: An odd smell around a pub could be from a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' gives AMORA, which goes 'round' the initials of 'public house'; 'pot' is an ancient jar, not cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a tall two-handled ancient jar, a kind of pot.

clue.text: Right to stop character in Star Trek film finding tooth

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to fill it, so R plugs the inside of the name

parts.note: Mr Spock is the Vulcan officer in Star Trek
ET is the Spielberg film about an extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A Star Trek character in a film finds a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprocket is a single projecting tooth on a wheel that engages a chain.

clue.text: Main part of site in leaf

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a leaf of a book is a page

explanation.surface: Something central to a location lies in some foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'site' is a website, not a building plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A homepage is the principal entry page of a website.

clue.text: Appealing without photo, it's to do with units of heredity

definitions.text: to do with units of heredity

indicators.note: without means the second word is removed from the first

parts.note: photogenic means appealing in pictures
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something attractive without pictures relates to genes.
explanation.definitionFit: Genic means relating to genes, the units of heredity.

clue.text: Talk feature, pay cut

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: cut means the word for pay loses its last letter

parts.note: a wage is pay

explanation.surface: A talk about a feature on a pay cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is an informal British word for a chat.

clue.text: FBI agent, good fellow

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A federal agent is a good fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: G-man is American slang for a government agent of the FBI.

clue.text: Option Tom exercised is disputed subject

indicators.note: exercised suggests the letters are worked about and moved

explanation.surface: Tom's taking up an option is a matter people argue about.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is a question open to debate with no settled answer.

clue.text: Lacks necessities

definitions.meaning: a verb: someone who ... something lacks it

explanation.definitionFit: Needs as a verb means requires for want of, and as a noun means requirements.

clue.text: Fast walk by demonstrators?

parts.note: fast is going without food, and a protest walk by those suffering is a march

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed but means going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunger march was a protest procession by the unemployed, as in 1930s Britain.
